name: Eli Lilly

header.one_liner: The incretin franchise: volume is exploding, price per unit is falling, and the multiple already assumes the volume wins.
header.thesis: Revenue grew 48% on 60% more volume and 13% lower prices. The base case fades growth to 18% a year and compresses the P/E from 32x to 24x, which beats the hurdle (10.1% a year), but the bear case loses 18% a year, so the probability-weighted return is about the hurdle. The central debate is price erosion versus volume.

base.eps_label: FY2026 non-GAAP EPS, midpoint of guidance $35.50 to $36.50 (includes $3.03 of Q2 acquired IPR&D)
base.rev_label: FY2026 revenue, midpoint of guidance $85B to $87B

rev_cagr.why: Q2 revenue +48%: volume +60%, price -13% (US price -3%, outside US -36%). Retatrutide BLA is planned for Q1 2027 and orforglipron (Foundayo) is launching. The base case fades growth from 48% toward the high teens as price erosion and comparables bite. This is the engine's judgment.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 37% on guided EPS including acquired IPR&D. Gross margin was 85.8%. The base case assumes slight leverage as R&D falls as a share of revenue (17% in Q2), offset by price erosion.

share_chg.why: Weighted diluted shares fell from 894.8M (H1) to 893.7M (Q2). The release does not state repurchases.

exit_pe.why: Current multiple is 32x. Large pharmaceutical growth names have historically traded between 16x and 30x. The base case assumes a growth-driven premium that narrows as volume growth slows. The bear case prices a patent-style cliff on pricing.

pillars.title: Volume is the story, price is the cost
pillars.claim: Volume +60% against price -13% means the franchise is growing by getting cheaper per dose and bigger in aggregate. The ex-US price drop of 36% is the leading indicator of where US pricing could go.
pillars.test: Does US realised price stay within -5% a year while volume grows above 30%?

pillars.title: Margins are very high and rising
pillars.claim: Non-GAAP gross margin 86.3% and operating margin about 39% after $2.8B of acquired IPR&D; R&D is only 17% of revenue.
pillars.test: Does gross margin stay above 85% as prices fall?

pillars.title: The pipeline widens the franchise
pillars.claim: Retatrutide has a complete obesity data package with BLA in Q1 2027; orforglipron was submitted for type 2 diabetes; new products added $98M to $201M each in the quarter.
pillars.test: Is the retatrutide BLA submitted on schedule?

pillars.title: Guidance was raised on revenue, not EPS
pillars.claim: Revenue guide rose $3B to $85B to $87B but EPS guide midpoint fell $0.25 because of $3.03 of IPR&D charges. Underlying EPS rose $2.78.

evidence.t: EPS guide $35.50 to $36.50 from $35.50 to $37.00; performance margin raised to 49% to 50.5%

pillars.test: Does acquired IPR&D stay a one-off or become a recurring charge?

variant.street: The market prices a long runway of incretin growth at 32x earnings and a $1.1T market cap.
variant.ours: The engine lands neutral: the base case clears the hurdle but the bear tail is fat. Three of four drivers are judgment, so this is the position to challenge hardest on price erosion and the multiple.
variant.could_be_wrong: If volume keeps compounding at 50% and price stabilises, the bull case is understated.
variant.would_change_mind: US realised price falling more than 8% a year, or retatrutide delayed beyond 2027.

moat.summary: Patent-protected incretin franchise with manufacturing scale; buyers (wholesalers and PBMs) and government pricing are the weak spot.
moat.detail: Existing Porter card (FY2025 10-K) rates Lilly Moderate because buyer power is high.

quality.leverage_note: Cash and debt not stated in the release.
quality.incentive_note: Acquired IPR&D of $3.36B in H1 is large; ask whether it is a recurring cost of staying ahead.

catalysts.label: Lilly Q3 2026 earnings (date not confirmed; typically late October or early November)
catalysts.note: Watch US price versus volume split.

catalysts.label: Retatrutide BLA submission planned for Q1 2027

tripwires.text: Realised price decline worse than -15% in a quarter

risks: Government pricing action and wholesaler concentration.

lenses.eisman: Volume +60% with price -13%: ask whether growth is being bought with price, and what the ex-US 36% decline implies for the US.
lenses.munger: Invert it: what kills this? A pricing reset that arrives faster than volume.
lenses.buffett: Wonderful business, but he would refuse to underwrite a three-year price path he cannot see; circle-of-competence test is hard.
lenses.hohn: Durable demand and pricing power are the test: price is falling, so durability rests on volume and the pipeline.

review.basis: Q2 2026 10-Q. Q3 is expected around 30 October (date not confirmed); this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: The incretin leader, growing 48% on one molecule. Volume is winning; price and policy decide how long the premium lasts.
review.model: Lilly discovers, makes and sells branded medicines. Tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity, is now the company.

how_it_earns.v: Incretins for diabetes and obesity. 80% of Q2 revenue.
Verzenio for breast cancer plus newer launches. Flat to low growth.

mix.note: Revenue only: Lilly reports one segment, so profit by product is not disclosed. Cardiometabolic, Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience are Lilly's own groupings.

rows.label: Cardiometabolic
rows.driver: Volume +60% group-wide; price down on access deals and China NRDL

rows.label: Oncology
rows.driver: Verzenio flat; newer launches add growth

review.position: One of two companies, with Novo Nordisk, that dominate obesity and diabetes incretins. Lilly is taking share: consensus has Novo's revenue falling in 2026 while Lilly's grows over a third.

moat.threat: Buyers are concentrated (PBMs, government). They take a growing share of the value through price.

what_numbers_say.t: Volume is doing all the work
what_numbers_say.d: Q2 revenue +48%: volume +60%, price -13%. Outside the US, price fell 36% as Mounjaro entered China's reimbursement list.
Gross margin 85.8% (+1.5 pts) on better production cost and mix. R&D fell to 17% of revenue as sales outgrew it.
Mounjaro and Zepbound were 65% of H1 revenue. Any setback to one molecule hits the whole company.
$13.3B spent on acquisitions in H1 2026, $2.0B more in July and a $2.8B deal pending. Acquired IPR&D was $2.8B in Q2.

balance.read: Leverage is still low against EBITDA, but debt rose $12.4B in six months to fund deals.
facts: Total debt $54.9B at 30 June, up from $42.5B
$10.1B undrawn credit facilities; $7.0B buyback authorisation left

flags.flag: Rebate estimate changes flattered US price
flags.evidence: MD&A: lower US realised prices were partially offset by adjustments to estimates for rebates and discounts. Gross-to-net reserves are judgment calls.

flags.flag: Acquired IPR&D is large and recurring
flags.evidence: $2.8B in Q2 and $3.4B in H1. Lilly includes it in non-GAAP EPS, which is the conservative choice, but it makes EPS lumpy.
Jardiance price set from 2026; Trulicity and Verzenio selected, effective 2028 (IRA).

forecast_basis.rev_cagr: Changed assumption: fades from 48% toward high teens as price cuts and comparisons bite
forecast_basis.margin_end: Judgment: operating leverage offset by price erosion
forecast_basis.share_chg: Trend: share count barely moves; buybacks offset dilution
forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: growth premium narrows as growth slows

base.story: Volume keeps compounding as access widens; price erosion slows; growth fades to the high teens and the multiple compresses.
base.needs: US price decline stays mild; orforglipron and retatrutide launch on time

downside.story: Policy and competition reset US price faster than volume grows; the market re-rates Lilly toward big-pharma multiples.
downside.needs: US price falling more than 8% a year, or a safety or supply setback

upside.story: Oral and next-generation launches open new patients; price stabilises and growth stays above 30%.
upside.needs: Retatrutide approved in 2027 and Medicare obesity coverage made permanent

risks.cause: Price falls faster than volume grows
risks.how: Wider access (Medicare bridge, cash-pay cuts, China NRDL) lowers price per dose. If volume growth slows first, revenue growth collapses.
Most-favoured-nation pricing and IRA negotiation pull US prices toward international levels, which are far lower.
Novo's next-generation and oral products, and illegal compounded copies, compete for the same patients.
65% of revenue is tirzepatide. A safety signal, supply problem or patent challenge would hit everything at once.
Debt-funded acquisitions are expensed as IPR&D. If the programmes fail, the cash is gone and leverage stays higher.

peer_read.why_premium: Lilly is the only large pharma growing revenue above 30%, with the highest EBITDA margin and return on capital in the group.
peer_read.why_not: Novo Nordisk sells the same class of drug at well under half of Lilly's forward P/E because its growth has stalled. That gap shows how much of Lilly's value depends on continued share gains.
peer_read.peers_note: Novo reports in DKK; ratios are computed in DKK and sizes converted to USD. Trailing pharma P/Es are distorted by acquired IPR&D, so NTM is the cleaner read.

questions: How much of the US price decline is policy, and how much is Lilly buying volume?
Is debt-funded deal-making a sign of a thin pipeline outside incretins?
Would you own this at Novo's multiple if growth halved?

review.title: Winning on volume, exposed on price
review.lead: We rate Eli Lilly {rating} with a 12-month target of {pt} ({upside} upside, {ret} total return against a cost of equity of {hurdle}). Lilly is winning the incretin market on volume, but price per dose is falling fast and our next-year EPS is {vs_cons} consensus: the shares already discount much of the good news.
review.call_reason: Leadership is priced in: the target implies {ret} over 12 months against a cost of equity of {hurdle}, with a fat tail if US prices reset.

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Q2 revenue grew 48% on 60% more volume and 13% lower prices. Mounjaro and Zepbound were 65% of H1 revenue: the growth is real, but it rests on one molecule.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: Patents, injectable manufacturing scale and a deep follow-on pipeline (orforglipron launched for obesity, retatrutide filing planned for Q1 2027) keep Lilly ahead. Buyers and governments, not rivals, are the weak spot.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: Gross margin rose to 85.8% even as prices fell, and R&D dropped to 17% of revenue. Operating leverage is strong for as long as volume grows faster than price falls.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Debt rose $12.4B in six months to $54.9B to fund $13.3B of acquisitions, with more pending. Leverage is still low against EBITDA, but more of the growth is now bought.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} Novo Nordisk sells the same class of drug at well under half of Lilly's forward P/E because its growth has stalled.

thesis_long: Lilly has won the first round of the obesity and diabetes market. Volume grew about 60% in the quarter, revenue outside the US rose 80%, and consensus has Novo Nordisk's revenue falling in 2026 while Lilly's grows by more than a third. Margins expanded despite lower prices. On execution there is little to criticise.

The debate is price. Realised prices fell 13% in Q2, and 36% outside the US as Mounjaro entered China's reimbursement list. Wider US access points the same way: the Medicare obesity bridge, lower cash-pay prices, and government price-setting for Jardiance now and Trulicity and Verzenio from 2028. Lilly's own filing notes that changes in rebate estimates softened the reported US price decline. As volume growth normalises, price erosion matters more each quarter.

Our base case fades revenue growth to the high teens and lets the multiple compress toward large-pharma levels, which leaves 12-month returns close to the cost of equity. The upside case needs the oral and next-generation launches to open new patient groups while price stabilises; the downside is a US price reset that arrives before volume growth slows. A US realised price decline worse than 8% a year, or a retatrutide delay, would turn us negative.

upside_risks.cause: Price stabilises while volume keeps compounding
upside_risks.how: If realised price declines ease as access widens, revenue growth stays above 30% and EPS runs well ahead of our base case.
Permanent coverage beyond the bridge programme would add a large, durable patient pool.
